A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CodeBrain framework and matching core experiments. All 37 pages of v1 and 43 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable; extracted text and rendered figures, tables, and equations support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CodeBrain results on ten EEG datasets, alongside component ablations, scaling experiments, pretraining analyses, and token visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds overlap-exclusion controls, channel robustness experiments, further ablations, and physiological token analyses.

M1.justification: The stated tokenizer objective gains temporal and frequency commitment penalties in Eq. 10. EEGSSM prose also changes RMSNorm to LayerNorm, although Figure 2 retains RMSNorm, leaving that implementation detail inconsistent. These are limited specification revisions within the retained two-stage tokenizer/SGConv/SWA framework.

E1.justification: The pretraining source and ten downstream datasets covering eight tasks remain the same. v2 Appendix L adds missing-channel input scenarios on FACED and SEED-V, masking 12.5%, 25%, and 50% of channels during finetuning. Other additions analyze retained datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark comparisons retain BENDR, BIOT, LaBraM, EEGPT, and CBraMod. The low-resource subset remains BIOT/LaBraM/CBraMod, and backbone alternatives remain CNN/LSTM/Transformer. The new channel experiment reuses CBraMod; CodeBrain (Excluding) is an internal ablation rather than a new external baseline.

E3.justification: v2 adds pretraining with TUEV/TUAB samples excluded, channel-masking and window/codebook/patch-size protocols, peak-memory measurement, and model settings spanning 3.86–146.75M parameters versus 6.82–15.17M. Sections 4.1–4.2 replace leave-one-session-out and linear-probing descriptions with trial splits and full finetuning, resolving conflicts with v1's appendices; this reporting correction does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds SGConv and gate removals in Table 3, physiological token case studies in Appendix A, pretraining-overlap controls in Appendix I, SWA-window/codebook/patch-size ablations in Appendix J, and channel robustness in Appendix L. Expanded model scaling also tests saturation at much larger capacities. Earlier class-specific-token, pretraining, and low-resource analyses are retained under changed appendix labels.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five random seeds and report means with standard deviations, including the same-seed component ablations. Added classification results continue this reporting format. No increased run counts, new confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises FACED CodeBrain Kappa from 0.5270 ± 0.0039 to 0.5406 ± 0.0084; several FACED masking and scaling results also change, while other main-table datasets retain their values. v2 adds exclusion-control, robustness, physiological-association, and larger-model results. Efficiency reporting changes SGConv from 8.74M parameters/15.17G FLOPs to 15.17M/8.74G and adds peak memory. These are reported revisions and additions, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Beyond v1's basic SSM derivation, v2 Appendix B adds an explicit FFT-convolution complexity proposition and proof. New Appendix C introduces a rate-distortion proposition and proof asserting that decoupled codebooks are no worse than mixed codebooks under independence, additive distortion, and a fixed total coding rate. This substantially expands the formal argument.

C1.justification: v2 removes the prominent claim of state-of-the-art performance under linear probing and presents generalization with full finetuning specified experimentally. It also redefines tokenizer novelty from the first EEG vector-quantization framework decoupling heterogeneous domains to the first EFM tokenizer providing domain-specific interpretability. These revise the scope of the empirical and novelty claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking tokens to physiological events, explaining one-second patches and equal-sized codebooks, and discussing channel robustness, overlap exclusion, and diminishing scaling returns. Conversely, v1 Appendix L's specific limitations concerning single-center bias, limited channel/data diversity, model scaling, and EEG-only scope are removed rather than relocated.

D1.justification: v2 adds EEGSSM configuration Table 6, including state size, bidirectionality, dimensions, and attention-window length, and clarifies channel-agnostic tokenizer embeddings and convolutional dynamic positional embeddings. It removes the pretraining-corpus version/date and explicit GPU counts and training times. Most hyperparameter tables remain unchanged; both versions still promise future code and weight release.

R1.justification: v2 adds VBH-GNN and MMCNN citations and removes references including XSleepNet, DMMR, Longformer, and RMSNorm. Novelty positioning emphasizes domain-specific interpretability, but the related-work taxonomy and principal relationships to existing EEG foundation models remain substantially intact.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around interpretability and generalization. Methodology combines the former preliminaries with the architecture overview. Appendices are reorganized, interpretability moves to the front, efficiency is separated from benchmark results, and limitations and broader impacts disappear. This exceeds simple renumbering or added scientific content.

P2.justification: v2 expands Figure 1 with heterogeneity examples and a radar chart, modifies architecture and token diagrams, expands ablation and scaling tables, and adds physiological, window-size, channel-robustness, and memory displays. Figure 3 expands model-size axes but duplicates FACED where v1 displayed SEED-V; detailed SEED-V scaling remains in the appendix.

improvement.justification: The overlap-exclusion control, broader ablations and robustness studies, and corrected protocol descriptions improve empirical scrutiny. However, Appendix C's high-rate approximation does not justify its asserted exact finite-codebook guarantee, Figure 3 duplicates FACED in place of SEED-V, and substantive limitations are removed. These benefits and reliability losses prevent a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
